newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia arrests 40 for church burnings - report.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia arrests 40 for church burnings - report.

text.p: Indonesian authorities have arrested 40 people for last week's arson attacks on churches in East Java in which at least five people were killed, the Jakarta Post said on Thursday.

The newspaper quoted Lieutenant General Syarwan Hamid, head of the armed forces' socio-political affairs unit, as saying that the 40 had been arrested in connection with the burnings, which authorities suspected were premeditated.
"The rioters said they held preparatory meetings for that purpose," Hamid was quoted as saying. But he said that no firm conclusions had yet been reached.

A statement from the Communion of Churches in Indonesia said that six people died and 25 churches were burned or damaged last week when thousands of Moslems attacked churches around Situbondo in East Java.
The government has said five were killed and local police reported that only nine churces were set on fire.
The riot broke out after a court hearing into alleged blasphemy against Islam in Situbondo, about 160 km (100 miles) east of Indonesia's second-largest city, Surabaya.
Several thousand people outside the court during the third hearing of the case called for the accused, a Moslem identified as Mohamad Saleh, to be sentenced immediately or handed over to the crowd.
The crowd went berserk after rumours spread that Saleh had escaped and taken sanctuary in a church.
About 85 percent of Indonesia's 190 million population is Moslem although the state ideology Pancasila recognises five mainstream religions and promotes religious tolerance.
